scope: Provider-initiated OIDC Back-Channel Logout, signed logout-token validation, distributed local-session revocation, replay resistance, pseudonymous Redis indexes, and fail-closed authenticated admission

priorDefect.control: Encrypted stateless web cookies with bounded provider refresh and RP-initiated logout
priorDefect.failureMode: A provider-initiated session termination had no authenticated path to invalidate a still-unexpired local web cookie across replicas.

implementedControls: a fixed Node-runtime POST endpoint accepts only bounded application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests with one bounded logout_token
logout tokens must be signed compact JWTs; encrypted tokens and algorithm negotiation are not accepted
verification pins the configured Keycloak issuer, client audience, exact asymmetric signing algorithm, and issuer-derived JWKS URL
JWKS retrieval uses one exact URL, a five-second timeout, disabled redirects, omitted credentials, no cache, and a 256 KiB response ceiling
logout tokens require iat, jti, the standard back-channel event, and sid or sub; nonce is prohibited
token age is limited to five minutes with a one-minute clock tolerance, and an explicit typ must be logout+jwt
multiple audiences require a matching authorized-party claim
the provider issuer, subject, session start, and optional sid are captured only from the already validated ID token inside the encrypted server cookie
provider identifiers and tokens are never exposed by the browser-readable session endpoint
Redis keys use an environment namespace plus domain-separated HMAC-SHA-256 indexes and contain no raw sub, sid, jti, token, organization, tenant, or financial value
one atomic Redis script records the replay marker and monotonic revocation cutoff
sid revokes only the targeted provider session; sub is used only when sid is absent and does not revoke a later login
revocation and replay TTLs exceed the corresponding local-session and logout-token validity windows
every server-rendered authenticated page and BFF cookie decoder checks the same revocation store before using upstream authority
missing provider-bound identity, matching revocation, malformed store state, or store unavailability removes provider credentials and fails authenticated admission closed
production configuration rejects a process-local store and requires bounded Redis connect/command behavior with one retry and no offline queue
valid first delivery and replay return the standard success status; invalid tokens and failed revocation writes return a non-success status without echoing identity or token data
the local Keycloak realm pins the exact development back-channel URL, requires sid, and Compose provides only the documented host-gateway development path

checks: exact dependency-policy validation across 20 package manifests
offline lockfile-bound validation of 209 production package licenses
production builds across all applicable workspace projects, including the dynamic Next.js back-channel route

idempotent replay success without divergent state

bounded form and media-type rejection before cryptographic work
revocation-store failure returns a non-success logout result
sid-scoped revocation preserves another session for the same subject
subject cutoff revokes earlier sessions and preserves a later login
missing or issuer-confused cookie identity fails before store use
store unavailability fails closed and removes provider access, refresh, and ID tokens
the shared server-session reader rejects an existing cookie after provider logout
one exact confidential Keycloak client
authorization-code flow and S256 PKCE retained
resource-owner password grants disabled
exact callback, web origin, and post-logout redirect
front-channel logout disabled
exact back-channel URL with sid required
offline-token revocation not silently expanded
explicit RS256 development signing pin
explicit local-only development revocation store
Compose host-gateway mapping for the documented host-process development endpoint

plannedCoverage: two independent Redis-backed store instances share one randomized test namespace
a logout recorded through one client is enforced through the second client
a different sid for the same subject remains valid
the same jti is classified as a replay across clients
exactly one replay and one sid key exist with only 64-character HMAC indexes
keys contain no raw synthetic subject, sid, or jti and have positive TTLs
liveRedisTestDefinition.interpretation: The production Redis adapter has an executable cross-client test definition. No live Redis assertion ran, so horizontal consistency is not claimed as observed evidence.

licenseAllowlist.result: Validated 209 production package licenses against lockfile SHA-256 24da6d00a98afa0a24b237065d99c886d10ebccc34f4dce5fe65260edf3fe0c6
replacementControls: derive every production and optional package from all lockfile importers and snapshots
include cross-platform optional packages independent of the current host installation
bind the sorted reviewed inventory to the full lockfile SHA-256
require exact sha512 lockfile integrity for every external package
validate offline without the pnpm package-store index
reject incomplete inventories and unreviewed exact license expressions
licenseAllowlist.interpretation: The earlier tooling defect is preserved above, but it no longer blocks the license decision. The replacement validator passed the complete 209-package production graph and is now part of pnpm verify.

browserRegression.interpretation: Provider credentials remain covered by browser non-disclosure tests. Provider-initiated logout requires an authorized live IdP and multi-replica topology beyond the local mocked browser harness.

operationalImpact.storeFailurePolicy: fail authenticated admission and logout action closed while leaving process liveness independent
operationalImpact.keyRotationEffect: SESSION_SECRET changes the cookie encryption and pseudonymous Redis indexes; rotation must drain old replicas and invalidate old cookies rather than run mixed secrets
operationalImpact.rollback: Do not restore provider-blind stateless production sessions. Drain authenticated traffic if necessary, restore the shared Redis path, and re-prove cross-replica invalidation before reopening.

remainingEvidenceAndOperationalRisks: Execute the live two-client Redis integration definition against the supported production Redis version and configuration.
Register and exercise the exact HTTPS back-channel URL on an authorized Keycloak client.
Prove account-console and administrator-initiated logout denial across at least two independently scheduled web replicas.
Exercise one-subject/two-sid targeting, sid-absent subject logout, later login, and replay through the real provider.
Exercise Redis startup failure, runtime failure, recovery, liveness behavior, and alert delivery without enabling fail-open behavior.
Exercise accepted/rejected clock boundaries and prove synchronized production clocks.
Exercise coordinated SESSION_SECRET and provider signing-key rotation with no mixed replica window.
Repeat the license and SBOM gates in authoritative hosted CI before release.
No production, staging, live Keycloak delivery, live Redis, multi-replica, recovery, rotation, clock, load, or alert result is claimed.
